newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Nov 15.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Energy Regulatory Board deferred to adjustments to domestic oil prices scheduled today pending the decision of the Department of Justice on the validity of the implementation of an oil price formula. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- About 200 angry residents at Olongapo, host city for the APEC Summit turned back 500 protesters marching towards the Subic Bay Freeport, the site of the November 25 forum, taunting and pushing them back in their first confrontation yesterday (INQUIRER,CHRONICLE)

- President Ramos has asssured leftist leader Filemon Lagman, arrested on Tuesday for the murder of a policeman in 1992, of due process and ordered Justice Minister Teofisto Guingona to handle the case (MALAYA)
- The arrested communist leader asked the Supreme Court to set him free and nullify the warrant of arrest and the murder charge against him (PHILIPPINE STAR)

- The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) announced dropping of the scheme under which 50 percent of an initial public offering (IPO) was alloted to brokers. It also announced the new composition of the stock index effective today that will include an all-share and banking/finance indices. (BUSINESSWORLD,PHILIPINE STAR,TIMES JOURNAL

- The Monetary Board, the policy-making body of the Philippine Central Bank (CB), will decide before year-end on the need to hike bank capital and to cut down reserve requirement, CB governor Gabriel Singson said at the 18th Asia-Pacific Foreign Exchange Assembly. Singson added the country's balance of payments (BOP) surplus as of yesterday reached $4 billion.

- The Philippines expects to have its sovereign credit rating upgraded next year as the domestic economy improves and is opened up further, President Ramos said at the 18th Asia-Pacific Foreign Exchange Assembly (INQUIRER)

- The former U.S. naval base at Subic Bay, now being groomed as a premier freeport in Southeast Asia and the site of the APEC Summit next week, is fast becoming a favorite destination of direct Taiwanese investments, top Taiwanese government officials said (BUSINESSDAILY)

- The U.S. government has warned the Philippines it may be moved back on to a U.S. "priority watch list" if it fails to enact a bill protecting intellectual property rights this year, U.S. Ambassador Thomas Hubbard said in a letter to Trade Minister Cesar Bautista. (STANDARD)
